exactText: I think this is mostly impossible: I think this is an exercise in predicting something that cannot be predicted.
sourceQuote: I think this is mostly impossible: I think this is an exercise in predicting something that cannot be predicted.
normalizedClaim: Precise prediction of which jobs and industries are exposed to AI displacement is largely impossible.
resolutionCriteria: Failure of detailed job-exposure models published in 2024–2026 to accurately forecast employment shifts by occupation by 2030, as measured against actual BLS or equivalent data.

exactText: the current market dynamics point to a future in which, as today’s supply crunch eases, frontier models move towards becoming commodity infrastructure, with all of the value built on top
sourceQuote: frontier models move towards becoming commodity infrastructure, with all of the value built on top
normalizedClaim: Frontier AI models will evolve into low-margin commodity infrastructure, with primary value accruing to applications and layers above them.
resolutionCriteria: Gross margins of pure model providers declining toward commodity levels while application-layer companies capture majority of AI value by 2032, per financial reports.

exactText: We will use AI to automate broad classes of stuff inside existing workflows and existing companies
sourceQuote: We will use AI to automate broad classes of stuff inside existing workflows and existing companies
normalizedClaim: AI will primarily automate tasks within existing company workflows rather than immediately replacing entire organizational structures.
resolutionCriteria: Majority of enterprise AI value realization through 2030 occurring via augmentation of existing processes rather than wholesale new company formation or process reinvention, per McKinsey/Gartner studies.

exactText: with every previous platform shift, the stuff that actually mattered was the stuff that wasn't even possible before and that no-one even imagined.
sourceQuote: the stuff that actually mattered was the stuff that wasn't even possible before and that no-one even imagined.
normalizedClaim: The highest-value AI applications will be novel use cases that were previously impossible rather than direct automation of existing tasks.
resolutionCriteria: By 2035, the largest economic contributions from AI stemming from new categories of activity rather than pure displacement of 2025-era jobs, as assessed in economic analyses.

exactText: I don’t think foundation models are a product. I don’t think a chatbot is a product. I think the value will be further up.
sourceQuote: I don’t think foundation models are a product. I don’t think a chatbot is a product. I think the value will be further up.
normalizedClaim: Foundation models and chatbots themselves will not capture the majority of long-term value; value will accrue higher in the stack.
resolutionCriteria: Market capitalization and profitability of pure-play model providers lagging behind application and platform layers by 2030.

exactText: any specific predictions about a particular field will only be correct by luck: it really does depend.
sourceQuote: any specific predictions about a particular field will only be correct by luck: it really does depend.
normalizedClaim: Specific field-by-field predictions of AI impact at this early stage will mostly succeed only by chance.
resolutionCriteria: Low accuracy rates of 2025–2026 granular industry AI-impact forecasts when evaluated against actual outcomes in 2030.

exactText: It’s going to be magic, and in 20 years time we’ll just say, well, of course that’s how it is. Computers have always done that.
sourceQuote: It’s going to be magic, and in 20 years time we’ll just say, well, of course that’s how it is.
normalizedClaim: In approximately 20 years, advanced AI capabilities will be taken for granted as ordinary features of computing.
resolutionCriteria: By ~2046, current frontier AI behaviors regarded as baseline expectations in everyday technology use, per cultural and technology histories.

exactText: Every big company gave everyone Copilot (or maybe ChatGPT or Claude) and a small number of people are using this a lot (some of whom actually increased their productivity), while a larger set of people are using it a couple of times a week and a lot of the rest of your company isn't really using it at all.
sourceQuote: a small number of people are using this a lot
normalizedClaim: Enterprise AI chatbot adoption remains highly uneven, with heavy use by a minority and limited use by most employees.
resolutionCriteria: Enterprise usage analytics continuing to show power-law distribution of AI tool engagement through 2028.

exactText: The state of AI today feels a lot like the web in 1997 or mobile in 2007: we know this is big but we don’t know how any of it is going to work.
sourceQuote: we know this is big but we don’t know how any of it is going to work.
normalizedClaim: As of late 2025, the long-term structure and successful applications of AI remain highly uncertain, analogous to the early web or early mobile eras.
resolutionCriteria: By 2030, the dominant business models and interface paradigms for AI still undergoing significant evolution rather than having stabilized.

exactText: I’ve argued at length that I think chatbots are a poor interface that will struggle to capture value up the stack
sourceQuote: chatbots are a poor interface that will struggle to capture value up the stack
normalizedClaim: Chatbot interfaces will struggle to capture significant long-term value higher in the software stack.
resolutionCriteria: By 2030, the majority of AI-driven revenue and usage occurring through non-chatbot interfaces (agents, embedded tools, vertical apps) rather than pure conversational chat.
